# Compatibility smoke matrix (early alpha)

This is a small, one-time benchmark, not a permanent test subsystem or a
claim about ecosystem-wide node compatibility. It answers one narrow
question: *can a representative set of normal Node-RED flow behaviors run
unchanged on top of this Temporal-backed execution runtime?* Every row
below reuses an existing automated spec or an existing manual demo as
evidence - no new automated specs and no new fixture files were added for
this benchmark (existing fixtures already covered every category below).

Base: Node-RED `5.0.7` (this fork's pinned upstream tag, per `AGENTS.md`),
Node.js `>=22.9`, `@temporalio/*` `1.24.0` (this package's `package.json`).

## Exact results (do not combine these into one invented percentage)

- **Node/runtime-mechanism cases** (capture layer, bootstrap, worker
  wiring, deploy lifecycle, credentials/context): **8/8 PASS**
- **Flow-pattern cases** (routing shapes a real flow author would build):
  **10/10 PASS**
- **Manual/external-gate cases** (not CI-run, human-executed): **2/2 PASS**
  (both re-run/re-verified as part of prior issues, not re-executed in
  this pass - see limitation notes below)
- **Combined full `@tbrandenburg` unit suite** (all specs, all
  categories, run fresh in this session):
  **156/156 passing** (`../../node_modules/.bin/mocha
  "test/unit/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/**/*_spec.js"
  --timeout 20000`)

These counts describe **only the tested cases below**. They must not be
read as "X% of Node-RED node types" or "X% of the Node-RED ecosystem" -
the tested population is a deliberately small, representative set of
flow patterns and runtime mechanisms, not a survey of contrib nodes.

## Manual contrib-node sanity gate (issue #48)

A small, one-time, manually-run gate (not CI, no permanent dependency added
to this repository) proving that runner B loads and executes ordinary
third-party `node-red-contrib-*` packages installed in its own `--user-dir`
(issue #46), through the normal editor→runner→Temporal path, with zero
node-specific adaptation in the runtime.

Packages installed in a disposable `npm init`'d directory outside this
repository's dependency tree (`/tmp/node-red-temporal-contrib`), each wired
into one small flow and started via `node-red-temporal start` against a
real local Temporal dev server (isolated Task Queue, not shared with CI):

| Package | Version | Node style | Behavior | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node-red-contrib-string` | 1.0.0 | legacy `on('input', function(msg){...})` (1-arg, no `done()`) | pure transform (`trim`) | **NODE_TIMEOUT** (see note) |
| `node-red-contrib-simple-gate` | 0.5.2 | legacy `on('input', function(msg){...})` (1-arg, no `done()`) | stateful open/close gate | **NODE_TIMEOUT** (see note) |
| `node-red-contrib-time-range-switch` | 1.2.0 | legacy `on('input', function(msg){...})` (1-arg, no `done()`) | time-window branching | **NODE_TIMEOUT** (see note) |
| `node-red-contrib-cron-plus` | 3.1.0 | modern `on('input', async function(msg, send, done){...})` (3-arg) | scheduler/stateful, calls `done()` explicitly | **PASS** |

Runner restart with the same `--user-dir` — **PASS**: stopped runner B,
restarted it against the same disposable userDir/Task Queue, re-triggered
`node-red-contrib-cron-plus`'s flow, and it completed identically without
reinstalling anything, proving the package came from normal Node-RED
installation state (not a one-process accident).

**Finding, not a contrib-node-specific bug:** the three `NODE_TIMEOUT`
results are not failures of those specific packages. Node-RED's own runtime
(`@node-red/runtime/lib/nodes/Node.js`'s `_emitInput`) only calls a node's
`done` callback when the node's `on('input', ...)` handler itself declares
a 3rd parameter and calls it. Legacy-API nodes (`on('input', function(msg)
{...})`, one argument, no `done()`) are a large share of the existing
`node-red-contrib-*` ecosystem (pre-dating Node-RED 1.0's `(msg, send,
done)` signature) and **never signal completion** to anything hooked on
`onComplete` - which is exactly what Capture (and therefore every
node-red-temporal Activity) waits on. This reproduced identically for all
three legacy-style packages tested and did not reproduce for the one
modern-API package tested, confirming the pattern rather than a
per-package fluke. A control run of the existing `demo/flows.json` (core
`http request`/`change`/`debug` nodes, all modern-API) against the exact
same runner/userDir/queue setup completed normally in under a second,
ruling out a regression in this session's own changes (issues #46/#47) as
the cause. This is a real, generic compatibility boundary of the
Activity-per-node execution model - not something this gate attempts to
fix - and is recorded here as a finding for a future issue (see "Follow-up
issues found" in the PR that introduced this section) rather than
expanded scope for #48 itself.

0 node-specific adaptations were made to the runtime to achieve the PASS
result above.

## Legacy (pre-1.0) input handler nodes (issue #53 resolution)

The `NODE_TIMEOUT` findings recorded above (issue #48) are now a **fast,
explicit compatibility error** instead of a silent 60s hang: `capture.js`
listens to Node-RED's own `postReceive` hook and reads
`node._expectedDoneCount` (an existing, unmodified upstream `Node.js`
per-instance counter, incremented only when a registered `input` handler
declares 3 parameters) - a generic, node-type-agnostic, read-only signal
for "does Node-RED expect a `done()` completion for this node invocation
at all". When it does not, and the invocation did not forward its message
internally (the same `z`-chain check subflow instance routing already
relies on - see `capture.js`'s `_isInternalTo`), the pending Activity
invocation is rejected immediately with `error.code ===
"LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE"` and any sends the node already made synchronously,
instead of waiting out the full configured node-execution timeout.

This is a **fail-fast compatibility boundary, not a completion mechanism**:
Node-RED gives no exact, generic signal for when a legacy handler's
*asynchronous* work (e.g. a `setTimeout`-deferred `send()`) finishes, so
Capture does not guess with a grace period or heuristic - it fails
immediately and explicitly instead of guessing. A genuinely synchronous
legacy node that sends everything before returning therefore also fails
fast today (its sends are still returned on the rejection for
observability) - this is the documented, deliberate trade-off (see plan
in issue #53), not a partial implementation.

**Regression protection for the one legitimate exception**: Node-RED's own
subflow instance wrapper node (`@node-red/runtime/lib/flows/Subflow.js`'s
`this.node.on("input", function(msg){ this.send(msg) })`) is *itself* a
1-arg, no-`done()` handler by upstream design - its own completion is
never observable directly, only via whatever internal node it forwards to
eventually completing. `capture.js` recognizes this purely structurally
(an internal-route flag set the same way `_isInternalTo` already
classifies subflow-internal hops, not a check on node type), so subflow
instances keep completing exactly as before - confirmed by the pre-existing
`workflows_spec.js` issue #23/#33 subflow specs, which needed no changes
and still pass unmodified.

**Re-run of the issue #48 manual gate**: live re-installs of the four
named contrib packages were not repeated in this environment (no network
egress available to install `node-red-contrib-*` packages from a
disposable directory during this change). Instead, per issue #53's step
8 fallback, the exact same three behaviors were reproduced with real
Node-RED-runtime, non-mocked, test-only probe nodes registered via the
genuine pre-1.0 `on("input", function(msg){...})` API in
`capture_spec.js` ("issue #53 L1"-"L5"):

| Case | Represents | New result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy handler, synchronous send, no `done()` | `node-red-contrib-string`, `node-red-contrib-simple-gate`, `node-red-contrib-time-range-switch` (sync portion) | **Fails fast** with `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE` (well under 1s, not 60s), sends still returned |
| Legacy handler, no send, no `done()` | same packages, no-op paths | **Fails fast** with `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE`, empty sends |
| Legacy handler, asynchronous (`setTimeout`) send, no `done()` | any legacy node doing real async work | **Fails fast** immediately (does not wait for the async send or the timeout); the later async send is safely ignored, not mis-attributed |
| Modern `(msg, send, done)` handler (sync, delayed, zero-send) | `node-red-contrib-cron-plus` | **Unchanged** - resolves via `onComplete` exactly as before |
| Modern handler that never calls `done()` (genuine hang) | n/a (this is a bug in that node, not a legacy-API distinction) | **Unchanged** - still times out with the ordinary `NODE_TIMEOUT`, not `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE` |

No contrib package versions were swapped or omitted to manufacture this
result; the fixtures reproduce the same handler-arity behaviors the four
real packages exhibited, without depending on network access.

## Explicitly unsupported

- **HTTP In / HTTP Response** — intentionally unsupported in the early alpha.
  These nodes depend on live Express `req`/`res` objects and are outside
  the durable serialization boundary. This does not apply to the outbound
  `http request` node, which is supported subject to Activity at-least-once
  semantics.

## Scope note

This matrix intentionally covers ~15-20 representative flow-pattern and
runtime-mechanism cases, reusing existing automated specs and existing
manual demos as evidence per issue #36's anti-monster constraints. It does
**not** attempt to test the broader Node-RED contrib ecosystem, and no
percentage or ratio above should be read as a claim about node types or
flows beyond what is explicitly listed.
